caution_findings.evidence_context: The paper proposes viral particle lysis, assembly/release interruption, and post-translational processing effects; only protease inhibition and binding are treated as direct assay-supported mechanisms.

extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism adjudication from local XML/PDF results and figure captions.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Ltc 1 directly inhibits recombinant DENV2 NS2B-NS3pro serine protease activity in low micromolar range and binds the protease in ELISA/docking-supported assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Docking is supportive only; the direct mechanism assignment rests on the biochemical protease inhibition and binding assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Ltc 1 reduces DENV2 replication in HepG2 cells in dose-response viral RNA assays and reduces viral particle/NS1 signals in immunostaining and western blot readouts.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is antiviral effect evidence, not by itself a direct molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Time-of-addition plaque assays show lower viral loads for pre-, simultaneous, and post-treatment, with stronger simultaneous and post-treatment effects; this supports a functional mode-of-action profile without resolving all proposed downstream mechanisms.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper's proposed viral-particle lysis and assembly/release interruption remain hypotheses requiring additional studies.
